newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINLAND SHOULD JOIN EMU DUE TO ECONOMICS - HETEMAKI.
newsitem.headline: FINLAND SHOULD JOIN EMU DUE TO ECONOMICS - HETEMAKI.

text.p: Economic grounds alone justify Finnish membership of Economic and Monetary Union (EMU), Martti Hetemaki, chief economist at the Finnish Ministry of Finance, told a news conference on Thursday.
Asked whether he would, based on economic grounds alone, decide for Finland to join EMU if it were up to him, he said:
"Yes, and I have always been of that opinion."
Many economists, particularly in Finland, have argued that EMU is a political project leading to a more centralised European Union which has little economic grounds.

The finance ministry at the news conference released its report on benefits and drawbacks of EMU which emphasised many beneficial sides of EMU and was optimistic about it, compared to staying outside.

Hetemaki said the report was purely economical and that it applied not only to Finland but to all EU member states. But he also said that Finland is today better suited for EMU than many other countries, including Germany.
Finland has gone through a dramatic adjustment in the early 1990s, he noted.
"We are in a better situation than most potential EMU members in central Europe like France and Germany," he said.

The report gave no quantitative estimate of benefits and drawbacks of EMU and throughout, it compared membership with a scenario of being outside EMU where more austerity would be needed than inside it.
"It is not possible to give any credible exact estimates about this issue," Hetemaki said.
The Finnish government has promised to give to parliament its account of the impact of EMU on Finland in the autumn of 1997 prior to the EU summit in 1998 where the fate of EMU will be determined.
The government has not specified whether it will be a proposal or a notification, but both options will be voted on and thus be issues of confidence.
